text: 卖淫在德国2002年合法化，当时的理由是：自古以来就没有哪个国家能通过禁止杜绝卖淫的，干脆合法化算了，为了保护这些性工作者，从此以后就是光明正大的纳税人了，不需要受皮条客的剥削了，还得上课，发证书，然后还要定期体检
en: Prostitution was legalised in Germany in 2002; the reasoning at the time was: no country throughout history has ever managed to eradicate prostitution through prohibition, so they might as well legalise it. To protect these sex workers, from then on they would be open and above-board taxpayers, no longer exploited by pimps, and would even attend classes, receive certificates, and undergo regular health check-ups.

text: 结果德国立刻变成欧洲大妓院，东欧的各种国家立刻跑来德国卖，价格立刻就崩了。

text: 而且旁边的法国也很奇葩，法国罚嫖客不罚娼妓，导致离边境近的来德国嫖。
en: Moreover, neighbouring France is also rather bizarre: France punishes the clients rather than the prostitutes, which drives those living near the border to come to Germany for paid sex.

text: 婚外情、出轨、养小三、包养情妇完全合法，不仅不影响离婚的财产分配，甚至私生子也可以继承遗产。
en: Extramarital affairs, infidelity, keeping a mistress, and supporting a mistress are completely legal; not only do they not affect the division of property in divorce, but even illegitimate children can inherit the estate.

text: 几乎所有的反驳者都是在用那种强迫的、非志愿的用钱换性举例子。
en: Almost all those who object do so by citing cases of forced, non-consensual exchanges of money for sex.

text: 但是这种主观自愿的用性换钱的他们就好像没看见一样。
en: But they act as if they simply do not see this kind of subjective, voluntary exchange of sex for money.

text: 说白了，反对卖淫的立足点就三个，家庭、贞洁、人人平等。
en: To put it plainly, the grounds for opposing prostitution are three: family, chastity, and equality for all.

text: 而在现实中，这些观念已经被消解的差不多了。
en: Yet in reality, these notions have already been all but dissolved.

en: Actually, the greatest harm of legalising prostitution is that vast numbers of practitioners flood in, standards keep rising, giving rise to corresponding training institutions and a specialised service industry for prostitution workers — analogous to today's Didi — and what does it ultimately look like?

text: 一个很有趣的现象。

text: 按照我在文中表述的核心内容：认可性神圣必然反对性交易，认可性自由必然支持性交易。
en: According to the core argument I set out in the article: to affirm the sacredness of sex necessarily means opposing sexual transaction, and to affirm sexual freedom necessarily means supporting sexual transaction.

text: 按理来说应该会有两波人反对我。

text: 一波是认为性神圣但是认可性交易。

text: 另一波是认为性自由但是反对性交易。
en: The other camp believes in sexual freedom yet opposes sexual transaction.

text: 但是从评论区肉眼粗糙统计，目前跑过来找角度和我争吵，甚至是诉诸动机，道德绑架，扣各种帽子试图诛心作者从而反对文章内容的，全是认为性自由但是反对性交易的那一波人。
en: But from a rough, eyeballed tally of the comments section, those who have come to pick fights with me, even resorting to impugning motives, moral coercion, and pinning every sort of label on me in an attempt to read the author's mind and thereby oppose the article's content — every single one of them belongs to the camp that believes in sexual freedom yet opposes sexual transaction.

text: 我记得之前有谈过这个问题。
en: I recall having discussed this issue before.

en: But I have found that Zhihu has now sunk to the point where many people cannot even understand what is being said; their minds are so simple that they can only register that your view differs from what I expected, therefore you are the enemy.

text: 好了接下来大家开始立场斗争模式。

text: 结论很简单，性的去神圣化必然导致性的自由化，而性的神圣化则必然导致性的拘束化。
en: The conclusion is simple: the desacralisation of sex necessarily leads to the liberalisation of sex, whereas the sacralisation of sex necessarily leads to the restriction of sex.

text: 这玩意儿本质上一体两面。
en: This thing is essentially two sides of the same coin.

text: 就是一个东西他不可能又神圣又随意。
en: It is simply that one thing cannot be both sacred and casual.

text: 而一旦性这个东西去神圣化，高度自由之后，他就是一个娱乐服务，本质上和你找人按摩找人陪聊陪玩是一样的。
en: Yet once sex is desacralised and made highly free, it becomes an entertainment service, essentially no different from hiring someone for a massage or for company and conversation or play.

text: 所以他必然可以交易。

text: 而一旦性神圣化，那么他就不可能那么自由，我们俩今天高兴看对眼了来一发，第二天所有人都当觉得稀松平常。
en: And once sex is sacralised, it cannot be so free: if the two of us fancy each other today and have a fling, by the next day everyone would find it utterly unremarkable.

text: 那他就不神圣。
en: Then it would not be sacred.

text: 所以你支持卖淫合法或是不合法，实际上是要你选择性在你这里到底是自由大于神圣还是神圣大于自由。
en: So whether you support the legalisation of prostitution or not ultimately comes down to your choosing, for yourself, whether freedom outweighs the sacred or the sacred outweighs freedom.

text: 我没有支持或者反对卖淫合法化的问题，我只是在告诉你，支持性自由却不允许卖淫，或者赞美性神圣却允许卖淫是不可能的事情。
en: I have no stance of supporting or opposing the legalisation of prostitution; I am merely telling you that it is impossible to support sexual freedom yet forbid prostitution, or to praise the sacredness of sex yet permit prostitution.

text: 在古代古人解决这个问题的办法，是男性角色的性不值钱所以这个问题不存在，而女性角色直接切割，人的性是神圣的，卖淫那部分开除人籍。

text: 对于性的问题还有一个很经典的吵架话题叫处女问题。

text: 也是很多人认识或故意认识不到。

text: 男性和处女发生性关系与同非处发生性关系，是享有了两性关系中更多的性权利，需要承担两性关系中更隆重更多的道德义务以及以此衍生的现实义务。

en: A man having sex with a non-virgin, as opposed to with a virgin, is the same; the man does not thereby enjoy fewer sexual rights within the relationship between the sexes, nor correspondingly reduce his male obligations within that relationship.

text: 这两个观点是互相排斥的，如果你支持其中一个就必须反对另外一个。

text: 同时两个观点自身不可拆分，比如你认为和处女发生性关系意味着更多的性权利，那么和处女发生性关系必然对应更多的道德义务和以此衍生的现实义务。

text: 在强调一边，我没有表达立场，我只是在梳理逻辑。
